title: Supported perfect approximation across an elementary distinguished square
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $W$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], meaning that every open cover of its point space has a finite subcover and its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact. Let $U\hookrightarrow W$ be a quasi-compact open subspace [def-a1-space-open-subspace] and $j:V\to W$ a representable etale morphism with $V$ an affine scheme. Suppose that $V\times_W Z\to Z$ is an isomorphism, where $Z$ is the reduced closed subspace with underlying subset $|W|\setminus|U|$ [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support], with point spaces as in [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Assume that $U\times_W V$ is quasi-compact. If $\mathsf A(U)$ holds, then $\mathsf A(W)$ holds, for the small-etale uniform supported perfect approximation property [def-sfb-space-supported-perfect-approximation].

proof.text: Use $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$, perfectness, support, and $b$-pseudo-coherence in the sense of the defining node. Etale restrictions are exact slice restrictions and preserve $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$. For a scheme chart $Y$, the exact faithful functor $\epsilon_Y^*$ identifies the Zariski and small-etale quasi-coherent derived categories, commutes with restriction to opens, and preserves and reflects $b$-pseudo-coherence and perfectness. Consequently support and the required cohomology isomorphisms and epimorphisms also transfer: on every open in the complement use exactness and faithfulness to preserve and detect zero kernels, cokernels and cohomology. These comparisons will be used on the schemes $V$ and $O=U\times_WV$; no representability of $U$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 08HN, induction step: comparison on V and U times_W V; Tags 071Q, 08H8, 08HE and 08HG.

proof.text: Here are the closure verifications used below. A perfect object has quasi-coherent cohomology: on its strictly perfect local models, terms are images of idempotents of finite free modules, hence quasi-coherent; kernel, image and cokernel closure then gives quasi-coherent cohomology, and the etale chart criterion descends it. If two objects of a triangle have quasi-coherent cohomology, its long exact sequence expresses the third cohomology as an extension of a kernel by a cokernel, so extension closure keeps it quasi-coherent. Perfect objects are closed under shifts, finite sums and triangles: restrict to scheme charts, use step 1 to pass to Zariski, apply the scheme thick-closure theorem, then detect perfectness back on the charts. Finally a perfect object is $b$-pseudo-coherent for every $b$, since the local identity map from a strictly perfect model is an approximation in every degree.

source.place: Tag 08HN, perfectness and cone assertions; Tag 08JL local-complex argument, spaces-properties.tex Tag 03M1, and cohomology.tex Tags 08CR and 08CS.

proof.text: Fix a closed $T\subseteq|W|$ with $W\setminus T\to W$ quasi-compact. Its base change to $U$ is quasi-compact, so choose a witness $r_U$ for $\mathsf A(U)$ and $T\cap|U|$. Enlarge it to be nonnegative: a $b$-pseudo-coherent approximation also works at any degree $c\ge b$, and the support condition in degrees $\ge b$ implies that in degrees $\ge c$. Put $T'=T\setminus|U|$. This is closed in $W$, is contained in the reduced complement $Z$, and $V\times_WT'\to T'$ is an isomorphism after giving $T'$ its reduced closed subspace structure. Put $C=V\setminus j^{-1}(T')$. The correct equality is $C=(V\setminus j^{-1}T)\cup O$. The first open is quasi-compact by the given definition of the quasi-compact immersion $W\setminus T\to W$, evaluated on the affine chart $V$; the second is quasi-compact by hypothesis. Thus $C$ has a finite affine open cover, of size $s\ge0$. Set $r=r_U+s$. All these choices depend on $W,T,U,V$, not on $m,E$.

source.place: Tag 08HN, first paragraph; union formula and choice r=r_U+s correct the printed formula and max bound.

proof.text: Fix $m$ and $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_W)$ satisfying the hypotheses for this $r$, and put $b=m-r$. There is an integer upper bound $h$ with $H^i(E)|_U=0$ for $i>h$. Indeed, each local strictly perfect approximation at degree $b$ gives such a bound on its domain; the etale images of these domains are open and cover $|U|$, so quasi-compactness gives finitely many bounds, whose maximum together with $b$ works. If $U$ is empty the assertion is vacuous. Prove the desired approximation for every such $E$ by induction on $\max(0,h-(m-s)+1)$. The base is $h<m-s$; in the step $h\ge m-s$, the new object will have upper bound $h-1$. This formulation also includes $E|_U=0$, for which one may choose $h=m-s-1$.

source.place: Tag 08HN, induction on the largest nonzero degree: use an upper bound instead to include the zero restriction.

proof.text: Suppose $h<m-s$. Then $H^i(E)|_U=0$ for $i\ge m-s$, and since $b\le m-s$, the high cohomology is supported on $T'$ in this range. On the affine scheme $V$, step 1 writes $E|_V\cong\epsilon_V^*E_0$, with $E_0\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{V,\mathrm{Zar}})$, $m$-pseudo-coherent by monotonicity from $b\le m$, and supported on $j^{-1}T'$ for $i\ge m-s$. The complement of that support has the $s$-affine cover of step 3. The affine approximation theorem therefore applies (it only requires support for $i\ge m-s+1$) and gives $B_0\to E_0$. Pulling back gives a perfect $B$ supported on $j^{-1}T'$ and $\beta:B\to E|_V$ with isomorphisms above $m$ and an epimorphism in degree $m$.

source.place: Tag 08HN base case and Tag 08HM (lemma-approximation-affine), via perfect.tex Tag 08EQ.

proof.text: Since $B|_O=0$, supported etale excision identifies $P=j_!B$ with $Rj_*B$, with $P|_V\cong B$ and $P|_U=0$. These restrictions form a cover of $W$: $U$ covers its open and $j$ is an isomorphism over its complement. Thus the local strictly perfect models show $P$ is perfect. The adjunction in the excision node turns $\beta$ into $v:P\to E$, whose restriction to $V$ is $\beta$ under the unit isomorphism. Exactness of $j_!$ and the sum-of-lifts stalk formula show $H^i(P)$ is supported on $T'$, hence on $T$. On $U$, both $P$ and $H^i(E)$ for $i\ge m$ vanish, because $s\ge0$ and $h<m-s$. On $V$, the cohomology maps are those of $\beta$. Consequently $v$ has the desired isomorphisms and epimorphism: geometric stalks preserve finite limits and colimits and detect mono-, epi- and isomorphisms. This completes the base case, including $s=0$.

source.place: Tag 08HN base case; proof of Tag 08HL (lemma-open) and Tag 08HK (lemma-pushforward-perfect), using Tag 08GG and the extension-by-zero stalk formula.

proof.text: Now suppose $h\ge m-s$. Then $h-r_U\ge m-s-r_U=b$. Restriction of the local approximations to the slice defining $U$, followed by monotonicity, makes $E|_U$ $(h-r_U)$-pseudo-coherent and supported on $T\cap|U|$ in degrees $\ge h-r_U$. Apply $\mathsf A(U)$ at degree $h$, obtaining $p:A\to E|_U$, with $A$ perfect supported on $T\cap|U|$, isomorphisms above $h$, and an epimorphism at $h$. In particular $H^i(A)=0$ for $i>h$. We use approximation at $h$, not at the fixed output degree $m$.

source.place: Tag 08HN induction step, choose approximation on U: corrected approximation degree h and bound r=r_U+s.

proof.text: The overlap $O\subset V$ is a quasi-compact open scheme. Also $V\setminus j^{-1}T$ is quasi-compact by the defining test on the affine chart $V$. Transfer $A|_O$ to the Zariski quasi-coherent derived category via step 1 (perfect objects are quasi-coherent by step 2). Apply supported affine stabilization to obtain a perfect $Q$ on $V$, supported on $j^{-1}T$, with $c:Q|_O\xrightarrow{\sim}(A\oplus A[1])|_O$. Apply affine perfect-map lifting to $p|_O\circ\mathrm{pr}_1\circ c:Q|_O\to E|_O$, after the same comparison. Replace $Q$ by the supplied perfect $Q_1$, with $\beta_1:Q_1\to Q$ an isomorphism on $O$ and $\gamma:Q_1\to E|_V$ satisfying $\gamma|_O=p|_O\circ\mathrm{pr}_1\circ c\circ\beta_1|_O$. The node explicitly preserves support, since $Q_1=Q\otimes^{\mathbf L}I$. Transfer back to the small-etale site; exact faithful comparison and its restriction isomorphism preserve this equation and every support and perfectness condition.

source.place: Tag 08HN induction step: perfect.tex Tags 08EK (lemma-lift-perfect-complex-plus-shift-support) and 08EH (lemma-lift-map); comparisons 071Q and 08HG.

proof.text: Use derived distinguished-square gluing with $A\oplus A[1]$ on $U$, $Q_1$ on $V$, the overlap isomorphism $(c\circ\beta_1|_O)^{-1}$ and compatible maps $p\circ\mathrm{pr}_1,\gamma$. It gives $a:R\to E$ with these restrictions. Perfectness and support on $T$ hold on this etale cover, hence globally by the local definition and stalk detection. Step 2 puts $R$ in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$. On $U$, $H^i(R)=H^i(A)\oplus H^{i+1}(A)$ vanishes for $i>h$, and $H^h(a)$ is surjective. All shifts here use $H^i(A[1])=H^{i+1}(A)$, as in the specified derived category.

source.place: Tag 08HN, apply Tag 08HB (lemma-glue) to objects and compatible maps.

proof.text: Complete $a$ to a triangle $R\to E\to E_1\to R[1]$. The perfect object $R$ is $(b+1)$-pseudo-coherent by its local identity approximations. Part (1) of the ringed-site triangle theorem therefore makes $E_1$ $b$-pseudo-coherent. Step 2 gives $E_1\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$. The exact cohomology sequence on $U$ gives $H^i(E_1)|_U=0$ for $i\ge h$: use the epimorphism in degree $h$ and vanishing of $R|_U,E|_U$ above $h$. Outside $T$, every cohomology of $R$ is zero, so this sequence identifies $H^i(E_1)$ there with $H^i(E)$; the same support bound in degrees $\ge b$ persists. Thus the induction hypothesis applies with upper bound $h-1$, yielding $v_1:P_1\to E_1$ with $P_1$ perfect supported on $T$, isomorphisms above $m$ and an epimorphism at $m$. The nonnegative induction parameter strictly decreased.

source.place: Tag 08HN, the cone E prime and induction; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08FV(1).

proof.text: Let $d:E_1\to R[1]$ be the boundary. Complete $d\circ v_1$ and rotate to get a triangle $R\to P\to P_1\xrightarrow{d\circ v_1}R[1]$. Apply TR3 to its rotation starting with $P_1\to R[1]$ and the corresponding rotation starting with $E_1\to R[1]$, with maps $v_1$ and $1_{R[1]}$. Shift back to obtain $v:P\to E$ and a morphism of the displayed triangles, with components $1_R,v,v_1,1_{R[1]}$. Step 2 gives perfectness of $P$. Restricting the upper triangle outside $T$, its outer terms have zero cohomology; exactness then gives zero cohomology of $P$ there. Thus $P$ is supported on $T$.

source.place: Tag 08HN, final morphism of distinguished triangles via TR3.

proof.text: Here is the endpoint diagram chase on a geometric stalk. For $i\ge m$, send $z\in H^i(E)$ to $z_1\in H^i(E_1)$ and lift $z_1$ through the surjection $H^i(v_1)$ to $x_1\in H^i(P_1)$. Its boundary in $H^{i+1}(R)$ is zero by the commuting diagram, so it lifts to $x\in H^i(P)$. The difference $z-H^i(v)x$ comes from $H^i(R)$; adjusting $x$ by that class proves surjectivity. For $i>m$, if $H^i(v)x=0$, injectivity of $H^i(v_1)$ says $x$ comes from $a\in H^i(R)$. This $a$ maps to zero in $H^i(E)$, so it is the boundary of $b_1\in H^{i-1}(E_1)$. Since $i-1\ge m$, lift $b_1$ through $H^{i-1}(v_1)$; exactness of the upper row then gives $x=0$. Geometric stalks preserve finite limits and colimits, so these are exact stalk sequences, and they detect the sheaf isomorphisms above $m$ and the epimorphism at $m$. Hence $v$ is the required approximation. The fixed $r=r_U+s$ works for all $m,E$, proving $\mathsf A(W)$.

source.place: Tag 08HN, expand the final easy diagram chase including the surjectivity endpoint.
